strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with per-stage scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local scaling/unscaling between each stage, exactly as in the reference. Each all-reduce is a separate dispatch (8 total), with full-sized payloads (world_size*1024 elements). Represents the baseline: maximum simplicity, no optimization, highest dispatch count but straightforward correctness.

strategies.name: Fused local-op batching between all-reduces
strategies.desc: Groups the scale/unscale operations into vectorized tensor operations to reduce kernel launches between all-reduces, using pre-computed scale vectors and in-place operations where possible. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but minimizes local compute overhead. Trades memory allocation (pre-computed scale arrays) for fewer local-op dispatches.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter plus all-gather decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce stage into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing scaling operations to happen on smaller intermediate chunks (1024 elements per rank instead of world_size*1024). Uses 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on smaller payloads and scaling happens on local shards only. Trades collective count for reduced computation redundancy.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapping with async collectives
strategies.desc: Launches all-reduce operations asynchronously where possible, overlapping communication of stage N with local computation (scaling) of stage N-1 results. Requires careful buffer management to avoid WAR hazards. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but hides local-op latency behind communication, improving total wall-clock time.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with intra-node fusion
strategies.desc:
Exploits the multi-node topology by performing intra-node reductions first (using shared memory or faster interconnect), then inter-node reductions, applying scale transformations at the hierarchical boundaries. Requires 16 collective operations (8 stages × 2 levels) but leverages hardware topology for bandwidth optimization when world_size=224 spans multiple nodes.
